title: Segment Anything
key_finding: Introduced the promptable Segment Anything Model (SAM) and the SA-1B dataset of over 1 billion masks on 11 million images; zero-shot segmentation was often competitive with fully supervised models.
wow_factor: One model trained on a billion masks can outline leaves, fruits and roots it has never seen, with no plant labels at all.

title: Adapting Vision Foundation Models for Plant Phenotyping
key_finding: Frozen MAE, DINO and DINOv2 backbones adapted with LoRA adapters or decoder tuning matched state-of-the-art task-specific models on leaf counting, instance segmentation and disease classification, though slightly worse in some scenarios.
wow_factor: A single frozen general-purpose backbone plus a few trainable parameters can serve several phenotyping tasks at once.
suggested_slide: Adapting generic foundation models to plants

title: SPROUT: A Scalable Diffusion Foundation Model for Multi-Crop Plant Phenotyping
key_finding: A pixel-space diffusion transformer pretrained on 2.6 million unlabeled open-field crop images (MCD-2.6M) improved over web-pretrained baselines on organ segmentation, crop-weed parsing, depth estimation and counting, with largest gains on dense structural tasks.
wow_factor: Plant science now has its own self-supervised foundation model trained on millions of field images, with code and data released.

title: OneRosette to predict them all: single plant prompting on a visual foundation model to segment symptomatic Arabidopsis thaliana time series
key_finding: Prompting a visual foundation model with a single annotated Arabidopsis image segmented infected-plant time series with Dice 0.977, transferred without fine-tuning to a second pathosystem (Dice 0.966), and gave r = -0.928 against a manual disease index.
wow_factor: One labelled image replaces hundreds of annotations, and the pipeline runs without a large GPU.

title: SAM-CLIP-Thermal: Leveraging large multimodal models for reliable and scalable annotation in thermal image segmentation for field plant phenotyping
key_finding: A SAM-CLIP pipeline combining zero-shot inference, few-shot fine-tuning and active learning segmented plants in thermal field images with mIoU 97.54% (LadyBird Brassica) and 76.94% (UGA Brassica); annotations were released publicly.
wow_factor: Foundation models now produce the training labels themselves, so new benchmark datasets can be built quickly.

title: Depth4PH: a vision foundation model-based framework for plant height estimation in agricultural scenes
topic: Monocular depth foundation models / plant height
key_finding: Fine-tuning Depth Anything V2 plus a prompt-based SAM 2 module estimated plant height from a single RGB image on a 350-plant multi-crop test set with R2 = 0.948 and RMSE 12.23 cm, against 22.62 cm RMSE for a conventional baseline.
wow_factor: A plain phone-grade camera can now measure 3D traits such as plant height that previously required LiDAR or rulers.

title: The Turning Point of 3D Plant Phenotyping: 3D Foundation Models Enable Minute-to-Second Cross-Crop Reconstruction and Beyond
topic: 3D foundation models / point clouds / Gaussian splatting
key_finding: Replacing COLMAP-style reconstruction with feed-forward 3D foundation models and Gaussian splatting cut average reconstruction time across 26 smartphone-captured plant sequences from 6.52 minutes to 1.58 seconds while maintaining phenotyping accuracy.
wow_factor: Roughly a 250-fold speed-up turns 3D plant phenotyping from an overnight batch job into a near real-time measurement.

title: Automated 3D Segmentation of Plant Organs via the Plant-MAE: A Self-Supervised Learning Framework
key_finding: A masked-autoencoder self-supervised framework for plant point clouds reached mean precision 92.08%, recall 88.50%, F1 89.80% and IoU 84.03%, beating PointNet++ and Point Transformer; on Pheno4D it matched them using half the training labels.
wow_factor: Self-supervision halves the expensive point-by-point 3D annotation needed for organ-level traits.

title: Breaking the field phenotyping bottleneck in maize with autonomous robots
key_finding: TerraSentia autonomous ground robots phenotyped nearly 200,000 experimental units in 142 research fields across the USA and Canada over five years, delivering ground-truth-validated plant height, ear height, stem diameter and leaf area index at scales sufficient to dissect genotype x nitrogen interactions.
wow_factor: Fleets of small robots already gather under-canopy breeding data at a scale no human field crew could match.

title: Global Wheat Head Detection 2021: An Improved Dataset for Benchmarking Wheat Head Detection Methods
key_finding: The Global Wheat Head Detection dataset grew from 193,634 labelled heads on 4,700 images (2020, 7 countries/institutions) to 275,187 heads from 16 institutions in 12 countries after relabelling and adding 1,722 images from 5 new countries.
wow_factor: An open, multi-continent benchmark plus a Kaggle competition pulled the computer-vision community into crop science.

title: UAV‐based deep transfer learning to improve grain yield prediction in winter wheat across temporal and spatial variability
topic: UAV multispectral deep learning / yield prediction
key_finding: A 1D-CNN trained on UAV multispectral traits failed when moved to a new year (R2 = -2.9), but deep transfer learning with 20% of target data restored R2 = 0.83; across locations, baseline R2 of -15.3 to -0.4 improved to 0.29-0.69 with 40% fine-tuning.
wow_factor: Transfer learning addresses the main failure mode of drone yield models, which is breaking in a new season or location.
suggested_slide: Drones + transfer learning beat G x E drift

title: Integrating multi-modal remote sensing, deep learning, and attention mechanisms for yield prediction in plant breeding experiments
topic: UAV hyperspectral + LiDAR multimodal deep learning
key_finding: An attention-based stacked-LSTM fusing UAV hyperspectral imagery, LiDAR point clouds and weather predicted plot-level maize yield in a genetics-focused trial with R2 of 0.82-0.93, and its temporal attention weights aligned with known growth stages.
wow_factor: The network learned on its own which growth stages matter, so interpretable AI agrees with plant physiology.

title: RhizoNet segments plant roots to assess biomass and growth for enabling self-driving labs
key_finding: RhizoNet, a Residual U-Net workflow with convex-hull post-processing, segmented root biomass in thousands of EcoFAB hydroponic scans across nutrient treatments and generalised across experiments, positioned as a component of self-driving labs.
wow_factor: Root growth, the hidden half of the plant, can be tracked automatically in closed-loop autonomous experiments.

title: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting
key_finding: GraphCast, a graph neural network trained on reanalysis, forecasts hundreds of variables 10 days ahead at 0.25 degree resolution in under 1 minute and outperformed the best operational deterministic system on 90% of 1,380 verification targets.
wow_factor: A 10-day global forecast that took supercomputer hours now runs in under a minute.

title: Probabilistic weather forecasting with machine learning
key_finding: GenCast, a diffusion-based ensemble model, produces 15-day global forecasts for over 80 variables at 0.25 degrees in 8 minutes and beat ECMWF's ENS ensemble on 97.2% of 1,320 targets, including extremes.
wow_factor: Probabilistic AI ensembles give breeders and agronomists risk distributions rather than a single forecast.

title: Neural general circulation models for weather and climate
key_finding: NeuralGCM couples a differentiable atmospheric dynamics solver with learned components, matching ML models at 1-10 days and ECMWF ensembles at 1-15 days, and tracking climate metrics for decades at orders-of-magnitude lower compute; the authors note it does not extrapolate to substantially different future climates.
wow_factor: The hybrid physics-plus-learning recipe that works for the atmosphere is the template for next-generation crop models.

title: A foundation model for the Earth system
key_finding: Aurora, a foundation model trained on over a million hours of diverse geophysical data, outperformed operational forecasts for air quality, ocean waves, tropical-cyclone tracks and high-resolution weather at orders of magnitude lower compute, and can be fine-tuned to new domains cheaply.
wow_factor: Pretraining and fine-tuning, the same pattern as language models, now applies to the whole Earth system and could be fine-tuned for agro-climate variables.
suggested_slide: Aurora: one model for the Earth system

title: How AI is helping 38 million farmers with advance weather predictions
venue: Google blog / UChicago Institute for Climate and Sustainable Growth
key_finding: In 2025, a blend of NeuralGCM, ECMWF's AIFS and historical data predicted Indian monsoon onset up to a month ahead, including an unusual mid-season dry spell, and forecasts were sent by SMS to 38 million farmers with India's Ministry of Agriculture.
wow_factor: An AI weather model went from a Nature paper to SMS messages for 38 million farmers within about a year.

title: Decision-oriented benchmarking to transform AI weather forecast access: Application to the Indian monsoon
topic: Decision-oriented evaluation of AI weather models for agriculture
key_finding: A benchmarking framework linking meteorology, AI and social science showed that AI weather models skilfully predict an agriculturally relevant local monsoon-onset index weeks ahead out-of-sample, and it informed model selection for the 2025 forecasts sent to 38 million farmers.
wow_factor: Models are evaluated on whether they improve a farmer's sowing decision, not only on global error scores.

title: Integrating data assimilation, crop model, and machine learning for winter wheat yield forecasting in the North China Plain
key_finding: Assimilating LAI and soil moisture into a crop model, adding weather forecasts, then stacking ML raised North China Plain winter-wheat yield forecasts from ACC 0.69 / MAPE 7.79% (1-3 months ahead) to ACC 0.97 / MAPE 1.74%.
wow_factor: Stacking ML on a data-assimilated crop model cut forecast MAPE from 7.79% to 1.74%, about a 4.5-fold reduction.
suggested_slide: Hybrid crop models: best of both worlds

title: NeuralCrop: Combining physics and machine learning for improved crop yield projections
topic: Differentiable hybrid global gridded crop models
key_finding: NeuralCrop, a differentiable hybrid global gridded crop model first trained to emulate a process-based model and then fine-tuned on observations, matched state-of-the-art models, reproduced yield anomalies better especially under drought, and ran orders of magnitude faster.
wow_factor: This is the NeuralGCM approach applied to crops: a differentiable crop model that learns from data and still respects physiology.

title: An agricultural digital twin for mandarins demonstrates the potential for individualized agriculture
key_finding: An Open-API digital twin for mandarins on Jeju Island (~185,000 ha) integrated regional, inter-orchard and intra-orchard data; intra-orchard variation explained fruit quality substantially more than inter-orchard variation.
wow_factor: Digital twins point toward individualized agriculture, in which each tree is managed like a patient in personalised medicine.

title: Data-driven crop growth simulation on time-varying generated images using multi-conditional generative adversarial networks
topic: Generative models for plant growth simulation
key_finding: A multi-conditional Wasserstein GAN generated realistic future images of Arabidopsis, cauliflower and faba bean-wheat mixtures from an early image, growth time and treatment; adding process-based simulated biomass as a condition improved traits derived from generated images.
wow_factor: Generative AI can show what a plot will look like weeks ahead under a different cultivar or sowing density.

title: LSTM-attention-guided graph neural networks for integrated genotype–Environment modeling in maize yield prediction
topic: G x E deep learning (genotype + weather graphs)
key_finding: Encoding weather with an LSTM and 437,214 SNPs as genotype nodes in an attention GNN, the best architecture predicted 2022 maize yield for unseen genotypes and environments with RMSE 2.212 and r = 0.695, reducing RMSE about 20% compared with the base graph and beating the G x E competition winner.
wow_factor: Graph neural networks place genotypes and environments in one network and predict new hybrids in new environments.
suggested_slide: Graph AI for G x E
verified_via: crossref abstract (Crossref 'new version' update, not a retraction)

title: Structured Multimodal Deep Learning improves Genomic Prediction in Future Environments
topic: Structured multimodal deep learning for genomic prediction in new environments
key_finding: The Structured Interaction Neural Network separates genetic, environmental and interaction effects and reached accuracy 0.63 for next-cycle maize yield against 0.43 for BLUP and 0.48 for a prior neural net, and lowered benchmark RMSE to 2.41 vs 2.46 Mg/ha.
wow_factor: Deep learning beat BLUP once statistical-genetics structure was built in, which counters the common view that DL does not help genomic prediction.
suggested_slide: When deep learning finally beats BLUP
